newsitem.title: USA: Former US sex crimes prosecutor charged with porn.
newsitem.headline: Former US sex crimes prosecutor charged with porn.

text.p: A former deputy district attorney who prosecuted sex crimes in California has been indicted on child pornography charges, authorities said Friday.

The 19-count indictment, filed in U.S. District Court in Sacramento, accused former Sacramento County Deputy District Attorney Pete Harned of transporting, receiving and possessing child pornography between July 1995 and July 1996.
Harned planned to plead not guilty to the federal charges at his arraignment in federal court later Friday, his attorney Clyde Blackmon said.
Blackmon declined further comment. "This matter is in litigation," he said. "I have nothing to say."
Harned, 37, worked at the District Attorney's office for 11 years, where he handled child pornography as well as homicide cases.
He was fired last summer after he was arrested on state charges involving child pornography. Harned pleaded not guilty to the state charges, Blackmon said.
The federal counts, which carry tougher penalties, will replace the state charges, officials said.

U.S. Attorney Paul Seave said child pornography files were discovered in Harned's home computer when it was taken in for repair. The computer store alerted law enforcement officers, who said they found a removable disk drive containing hundreds of child pornography files during a search of Harned's home.
Authorities alleged that Harned used an online computer service to receive and send many of the images.

Under the federal indictment, Harned faces 11 counts of receiving child pornography, seven counts of transporting child pornography and one count of possessing "depictions of minors engaged in explicit sexual activity."
If convicted, Harned could receive up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine on each count.
